title: Subsets
oneLinerQuestion: Return the power set (all subsets) of a set of unique elements.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Subsets problem requires generating the complete power set of an array of unique integers. For an array containing N elements, every element independently presents a binary decision: it is either included in a given subset or excluded, leading to exactly 2^N possible subset combinations. This mathematical property maps directly to a binary decision tree traversed via Depth-First Search (DFS) and Backtracking, where each level of recursion corresponds to one element in the array.

- Step 1: Result Storage & Recursive Setup — We initialize an empty array 'result = []' to hold all generated subsets, and define a recursive helper function backtrack(index, currentSubset), starting at index 0 with an empty currentSubset = [].

- Step 2: Base Case & Leaf State Recording — When 'index === nums.length', the algorithm has evaluated inclusion/exclusion decisions for every element in the array, reaching a leaf node in the recursion tree. We push a deep copy of currentSubset (e.g., `[...currentSubset]`) into 'result' and return to backtrack.

- Step 3: Decision Branch 1 (Include Current Element) — To explore the universe of subsets containing nums[index], we append nums[index] to currentSubset and recursively proceed to the next position: backtrack(index + 1, currentSubset).

- Step 4: State Backtracking & Cleanup — Upon returning from the inclusion branch, we pop the last added element from currentSubset to restore its state before exploring alternative paths.

- Step 5: Decision Branch 2 (Exclude Current Element) — To explore all subsets that omit nums[index], we call backtrack(index + 1, currentSubset) without adding nums[index] to the current subset.

- Step 6: Termination & Output — Once all binary branches resolve, the traversal finishes and 'result' contains all 2^N unique subsets, including the empty set and the full array.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N * 2^N) because there are 2^N total subsets generated, and copying each subset of average length N/2 into the result array takes O(N) operations. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space representing the maximum recursion call-stack depth and the temporary subset buffer.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION subsets(nums):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(i, curr):
        IF i == LENGTH(nums) THEN APPEND COPY(curr) TO res; RETURN
        APPEND nums[i] TO curr
        backtrack(i + 1, curr)
        POP curr
        backtrack(i + 1, curr)
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, [])
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
